chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ali ibn Ishaq, from Sahl ibn al-Yasa', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever spends the night on a roof that is not enclosed (by a wall), and something hits him, let him not blame anyone but himself.'

key_terms.سَطْحٍ: Roof or flat surface of a building

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on sleeping on an unenclosed roof?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the principle of *al-ghurm bi al-ghurm* (liability follows the cause) in domestic architecture, emphasizing that negligence in securing one's living space transfers full responsibility for accidental harm to the individual. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is often cited to illustrate the broader legal maxim that one is accountable for foreseeable risks arising from their own choices, provided no external party is at fault. It serves as a practical guideline for urban living in early Islamic contexts, linking physical safety directly to moral and legal accountability.
